            A certificate in this input verifies another certificate's signature, but it is not a CA certificate: its BasicConstraints extension is missing or does not set CA:TRUE. Certification path validation does not accept such a certificate as the issuer of another certificate. The signature itself still verifies.

            The certificate names its subject only in the Common Name and has no Subject Alternative Name extension. Modern TLS clients ignore the Common Name when they match host names.
